intro: Land ownership around Grant Town carries the same layered history as much of Marion County: coal reserved to mining interests, surface held separately, and oil and gas rights frequently split off in yet another transaction. A mineral owner here needs the actual deed history, not a general assumption, to know what they hold.

sections.heading: A company town's layered mineral history
paragraphs: Grant Town's identity is tied to coal, but the oil and gas rights under the same ground followed a separate ownership path in many cases. We trace the reservation language in your family's deed to confirm what estate remains available.

sections.heading: Small tracts, real fractional shares
paragraphs: As with much of the surrounding area, Grant Town mineral interests have typically split among heirs over multiple generations. It's common to find a small tract with six or more co-owners, several living outside West Virginia.
